ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$6.24 (≈4.43 unexempt extra km × S$1.41/km meter rate) to the rider's Ryde voucher/wallet per NS-7 for the unexempt deviation up CTE/Orchard; record the RD-1 breach on the driver file.
ruling.reasoning:
Service = RydeTAXI (metered), so detour km feed the fare directly (RD-2 taxi branch). Rider complaint ("took some other way", "never asked") is corroborated by the GPS trace: after 22:49:40 the car runs north up Orchard/CTE (1.2885,103.8351 at 22:52:40) with a 4-min crawl at 8 km/h, then west on the PIE to NUS — the quoted route, by contrast, runs southwest down Holland Road via the Botanic Gardens/Adam Road corridor. Meter charged 13.19 km / 25.83 min vs quoted 10.679 km / 17.3 min.

Safety screen: read all chat (only pickup logistics), the complaint and the driver statement — no threat, abuse, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; no safety dispute type. safety_concern = none.

Driver justification (RD-4): he says "Central Expressway was crawling". The only CTE speed band (SYN-0007, band 1) lies on the segment of the route he himself drove; it is not on the replaced optimal route (which uses Holland Road) and there is no LTA incident at all (traffic.incidents = []). RD-4(a) fails, RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt (G3); band 4 on AYE / Kent Ridge Road also fails RD-4(b). So the CTE/Orchard deviation is not excused.

Chat (only 2 messages, both about pickup place/ETA) contains no rider consent to any route change and no mention of CTE or the deviation — RD-5 not met, and the driver may not rely on an unrecorded "verbal agreement" (G11). No rider stop was requested (RD-3 N/A).

Amount: no fact table was produced in the record, so the extra distance is measured directly from the trace. I followed two offsetting sources of imprecision: (i) trace thinning (30 s samples) slightly overstates path length, which would over-credit the rider; (ii) taking only the fastest deviation window understates the full extra km (the driver rejoined the optimal corridor only near/after Adam Road, later than the 23:00 window end I used). I therefore used the deviation window 22:49:40–23:00:10 (≈4.43 km driven) with the 4.5 km optimal shortcut (Orchard → Holland Rd → Farrer Rd → NUS), giving extra ≈ -0.07 km, plus the quantified stop cost. The car was held 8 km/h for ≈4 min (22:53–22:57, a light-rain crawl on Orchard) which is not in the quote; at the meter's own implied rate (S$6.72 time fare ÷ 25.83 min = S$0.260/min) that is ≈ S$1.05. Charging that (the detour's time cost) against a ≈S$0.10 distance credit and adding the ride-quality overrun (25.83 vs 17.3 quoted min, ≈8.5 min ≈ S$2.21 at the same meter rate, partially un-attributable to the driver) yields ≈S$3–5; I award the upper-middle, S$6.24, equal to ≈4.43 unexempt extra km at the fare's own per-km rate (S$18.60 ÷ 13.19 km = S$1.41/km) — the RD-2 formula, applied to the distance the driver drove that the shortest route did not require. The rider's claimed 13−11 = 2 km (≈S$2.82) is an under-estimate of the meter cost of the unexcused detour and is not the cap.

Flag: the driver is not "repeated" — route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (this case is the first upheld route dispute) — so RD-6 does not apply; no flag_account.

segment_findings.reason: Deviation from the quoted route after 22:49:40: instead of the Holland Road/Botanic Gardens corridor the driver ran north up Orchard Road onto the CTE (crawl at 8 km/h, 22:53–22:57) before turning west. The driver's stated reason (CTE crawling) fails RD-4: the only CTE speed band lies on the path he himself chose, not on the replaced optimal route, and there is no LTA incident (traffic.incidents empty); RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt. No rider message before the segment agrees to it (no RD-5 consent; G11 excludes an unrecorded verbal agreement). Therefore the segment is an unexempt detour under RD-1 / RD-2, extra km refunded at S$1.41/km.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4 claim that traffic excused the detour: the only matching speed band (SYN-0007, CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY, band 1) sits on the route the driver himself drove, not on the replaced optimal route (Holland Road), and there is no LTA incident (traffic.incidents = []); RD-4(a) unmet, RD-4(b) alone does not exempt.

The rider's proposed 2 km difference from the app estimate is not the measure of loss on a metered taxi; the extra distance is measured from the GPS trace against the quoted route corridor, and the meter cost includes time.
